1.why: The UI uses a clean sans-serif typeface with comfortable line height and letter-spaced code text, although body letter spacing is standard rather than notably generous.

2.why: No instruction text uses italics or all-caps (the only all-caps string is the secret value itself), and no screen presents a dense wall of text.

3.why: All content sits in a narrow single-column card with large full-width buttons, which reads well and should reflow cleanly at phone width.

4.why: Most prompts are short plain sentences, but the setup screen's paragraph introduces jargon such as 'TOTP', '30-second windows' and 'provisioning' that is not plain language.

5.why: Only the phone field shows an example format placeholder (+1 555 010 0184); the email and six-digit code fields display no example of what the expected input should look like.

6.why: The longest text a user must read is the four-line instructional paragraph on the setup screen, so no screen forces the user through a long block of text.

7.why: The 16-character secret JBSWY3DPEHPK3PXP is shown only as static text with no copy button, so the user must transcribe it into their authenticator app by hand.

8.why: The enrolment screen offers only the 'Manual setup secret' string; no QR code or equivalent alternative to manual entry is presented anywhere.

9.why: The fields are ordinary labelled inputs with no visible autocomplete or one-time-code hints, so autofill and password-manager support can neither be confirmed nor ruled out from the screenshots.

10.why: Each screen has a bold heading and a single full-width blue primary button, although the equally large red 'Sign out' button on the settings screen slightly competes for attention.

11.why: Each step requests a single primary task (Continue, Verify identity, Activate authenticator), with secondary navigation limited to 'Back to settings' and 'Sign out'.

12.why: Success-path banners explain what happened and what to do next, but after a failed activation the screen only says 'Verification could not be completed.' without stating what comes next.

13.why: The form remains editable with the button active after the error so retry is possible without stated penalty, but there are no controls to reveal, hide, or re-request a code.

14.why: The error 'Verification could not be completed.' is non-blaming but neither explains the actual problem (wrong or expired code) nor tells the user how to fix it.

15.why: The verification code 'expires in five minutes' and TOTP codes rotate on 30-second windows, so time limits are explicitly imposed on reading and entering codes.
